faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a payroll officer in 2026?
faqs.a: Under the Clerks—Private Sector Award, rates range from $29.45 (Level 2 Year 1) to $33.99 (Level 5) per hour from 1 July 2026. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week (typically 38) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $31.11 × 38 × 52 = $61,469.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Payroll Officer Salary in 2026

If you are looking up a **payroll officer salary** in Australia, the starting point is the Clerks—Private Sector Award 2020 (MA000002), which covers most private-sector payroll roles. From the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026, award minimum rates increased by 4.75%, following the Fair Work Commission’s Annual Wage Review. The National Minimum Wage also rose to $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week. However, payroll officers are typically classified at higher award levels, so their minimum pay is above the national minimum.

## Award Minimum Rates for Payroll Officers

The Clerks Award does not have a specific “payroll officer” classification. Instead, duties determine the level. According to Schedule A of the award, payroll work appears at four levels:

- **Level 2** – Initial processing and recording of payroll data, working in a payroll file. Year 1: $29.45 per hour; Year 2: $30.00 per hour.
- **Level 3** – Calculating and maintaining wage and salary records. $31.11 per hour.
- **Level 4** – Calculating wage or salary requirements, completing payroll data for authorisation, and advising on conditions, workers compensation and superannuation. $32.67 per hour.
- **Level 5** – Administering the organisation’s salary and payroll requirements, including executive packages. $33.99 per hour.

These rates are from Table 3 of the award. A full-time employee works an average of 38 hours per week, so the weekly rate is the hourly rate multiplied by 38. For example, a Level 3 payroll officer earns $1,182.10 per week ($31.11 × 38).

## Casual Loading and Fortnightly Pay

Casual employees under the Clerks Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate (clause 11.1). This compensates for entitlements casuals do not receive, such as paid leave. For a Level 3 casual payroll officer, the minimum hourly rate becomes $38.89 ($31.11 × 1.25). The loading is applied to the base rate, not to a rate that already includes it – our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains the calculation.

When working out a fortnightly pay, simply double the weekly figure. A full-time Level 3 payroll officer earns $2,364.20 per fortnight before tax. Casual employees may be paid per engagement, but the minimum engagement is three hours (clause 11.4).

## Annual Salary and Tax Estimates

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time payroll officer on 38 hours per week:

- Level 2 Year 1: $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,193 per year
- Level 3: $31.11 × 38 × 52 = $61,469 per year
- Level 4: $32.67 × 38 × 52 = $64,553 per year
- Level 5: $33.99 × 38 × 52 = $67,174 per year

These figures are gross. After applying the 2026–27 resident tax rates (tax-free threshold to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, etc.) plus the 2% Medicare levy, take-home pay for a Level 3 payroll officer is approximately $51,357 per year, or $988 per week. The Australian Taxation Office sets the tax scales, and our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides a detailed breakdown.

Superannuation is paid on top of the base salary. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a Level 3 payroll officer, that adds about $7,376 per year in employer contributions. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## How to Use the Hourly to Annual Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter a base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading. It then shows the annual, weekly, fortnightly, and monthly figures based on a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Remember: the calculator assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. For award-specific rates, always check the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

## Market Rates vs Award Minimums

The award rates are legal minimums. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2025 data), the median full-time earnings for Payroll Clerks (ANZSCO 5513) were $1,606 per week, or about $44 per hour – well above the Level 3 minimum of $31.11. This reflects experience, enterprise agreements, and individual arrangements. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for all full-time adults was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. Market rates vary by location and industry.
